subject.title: [Feature]: Cron should distinguish execution success from delivery failure and show warning instead of error

question: Should successful cron execution followed by failed post-run delivery persist as a first-class `warning` run status, or as `status=ok` with delivery failure shown through delivery fields and UI presentation?
rationale: Both open implementation paths can remove the false execution-failure signal, but the choice changes public status semantics, backoff/alert behavior, API schemas, UI filters, and external consumer expectations.

options.title: Approve ok plus delivery fields
options.body: Land the narrower split so execution remains `ok` and operators detect delivery failure through `deliveryStatus`, `lastDeliveryError`, and diagnostics.

options.title: Adopt first-class warning
options.body: Land a broader warning-state contract only after updating storage, Gateway schema, CLI/UI filters, docs, and compatibility proof.

options.title: Keep error semantics
options.body: Reject the split for now so delivery-only failures continue to drive `status=error`, backoff, and failure alerts.

recommendation.title: Approve ok plus delivery fields
recommendation.body: Land the narrower split so execution remains `ok` and operators detect delivery failure through `deliveryStatus`, `lastDeliveryError`, and diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent broad cron status/schema work makes this the strongest available owner for the cross-surface status semantics decision.
